title: 谁在给谁付钱？人工智能热潮（或泡沫）背后的循环资金机器
content:
Who's paying whom? The circular money machine behind the AI boom (or bubble)
Swati Mestri
Scientific Editor
Andrew Zinin
Chief Editor
Imagine a company that sells you equipment, invests money in your business and then rents back what you build with it. It's your supplier, your investor and your customer all at once.
That's known as circular financing.
Many artificial intelligence (AI) companies, including Microsoft, Amazon, Google and Nvidia, have adopted a version of this opaque method of financing.
A chip supplier invests in a customer such as a data center builder, the customer spends the money on the supplier's chips, and both companies report growth.
One central bank analysis found that 55.2% of investments in AI firms came from other AI firms.
What's not clear to investors or the market is how much of this AI boom is being driven by real, end-user demand—and how much might be a bubble.
It all comes back to Nvidia
Take Nvidia. The world's leading chipmaker is investing in ChatGPT owner OpenAI to support data centers filled with Nvidia chips.
Nvidia will invest US$30 billion in a private funding round for OpenAI and provide a guarantee of up to US$105 billion for an OpenAI data center in Ohio. It will also invest in the company building it.
That helps OpenAI remain Nvidia's best customer, but it also raises the question: Is the chipmaker propping up the market?
Nvidia has invested in other AI firms as well, including up to US$10 billion in Anthropic, the developer of Claude.
It bought US$2 billion in shares in cloud provider CoreWeave to help it speed up the build-out of AI factories that use Nvidia technology.
In total, Nvidia made more than 50 different investment deals in AI companies in 2024 alone.
Some of those deals are staged over years or still open-ended. But these circular deals help the AI build-out move faster than it could without Nvidia's financing.
The Australian story—Firmus
Data center builder Firmus—which last week abandoned plans to list on the Australian Securities Exchange—provides the local example. Nvidia wears all three hats for Firmus:
- Investor: Nvidia first invested in Firmus Technologies through the company's A$330 million capital raise in September 2025 to finance data centers in Tasmania. It then participated as an existing investor in two further funding rounds, one in April 2026 and Firmus' US$2 billion funding round in August 2026. Nvidia did not disclose how much it invested.
- Supplier: Firmus plans to build data centers using Nvidia's DSX AI factory platform, which combines chips, networking and software to provide computing capacity.
- Customer: Firmus signed Nvidia as a customer for its data center in Batam, Indonesia, in a deal worth up to US$30 billion over six years. Meanwhile, OpenAI (with its existing relationship with Nvidia) has been named as an anchor customer at Firmus' Malaysian data centers.
These circular deals also concentrate risk
The same loop concentrates risk. With Nvidia acting as investor, supplier and financier across the AI sector, trouble at one firm can spread quickly to the others. It also complicates valuations.
For instance, OpenAI's method of reporting revenue has been questioned. Its shares were hit last week when the Financial Times reported its annualized revenue was US$20 billion less than the company had suggested.
The Reserve Bank of Australia warned in its recent Financial Stability Review that there are "pockets" of higher-risk companies, including those using opaque or circular funding arrangements, where chipmakers provide financing to the companies that purchase their products.
Warning about the possibility of the AI bubble bursting, the RBA said, "One possible trigger could be a shift in sentiment toward the AI investment boom, which is increasingly fueled by expectations of sustained rapid earnings growth and a debt-financing cycle that is becoming more opaque and circular."
The concern is that nearly all the gains in the U.S. stock market have been driven by AI companies.
On Wall Street, chipmakers have contributed around 70% of the total gains in 2026 for the S&P 500, and Nvidia is now the index's largest single company at about 8.06% of the index.
This makes the market fragile. If investors begin doubting that OpenAI and similar customers can earn enough revenue from customers to meet their commitments, Nvidia would be hit on two fronts: first, via lower expected sales, and second, via its financing exposure to those same companies. That would drag down the whole market due to Nvidia's heavy weighting in the key index.
Australians would feel it too. Nearly 90% of households are exposed to AI stocks due to the U.S. shares held through their retirement funds.
A question of timing
None of this means the AI boom is fake. The issue is timing.
Nvidia, OpenAI and Firmus are betting that future revenue from users and businesses will grow fast enough to pay for today's massive data center build-out. Until then, investors, lenders and the companies' investments in one another fill the financing gap.
There is a historical comparison with the 1990s telecom boom. In what was then called the "New Economy," equipment makers such as Cisco Systems financed customers to buy their equipment. Too much fiber was laid too soon, and investors lost heavily when the stock market bubble burst.
But that fiber lasted decades. The newest AI chips have a shelf life of only a few years. If the expected revenue and demand from businesses and consumers arrive late or fall below forecasts, shareholders and retirement funds will bear the losses.

report.summary: 英伟达等巨头借循环融资推高AI热潮，繁荣背后暗藏泡沫风险
report.background: 这一轮AI基建投资中，芯片供应商、云厂商与模型公司之间形成了"你买我芯片、我投你公司"的循环融资结构。据一家央行分析，投向AI企业的资金中有55.2%来自其他AI企业。英伟达2024年完成50多笔AI投资，既是OpenAI、Anthropic、CoreWeave的股东，又是它们的供应商，还充当客户。这种模式加速了数据中心建设，却也让外界难以判断：AI热潮究竟来自真实终端需求，还是被资本自我循环放大。澳大利亚储备银行已就此发出金融稳定警告。
key_points: 循环融资指供应商同时扮演投资者、供应商和客户：芯片厂投资数据中心，后者用这笔钱买它的芯片，双方财报同时“增长”。
英伟达向OpenAI投资300亿美元，并为俄亥俄州数据中心提供最高1050亿美元担保；此外还投资Anthropic、CoreWeave等，2024年完成50多笔AI投资。
澳洲数据中心商Firmus是典型案例：英伟达三轮参投、供应DSX平台，又签下最高300亿美元采购协议，OpenAI则被列为马来西亚项目锚定客户。
风险高度集中：一旦某家公司出问题，风险就会沿投资链迅速传导。OpenAI被曝年化收入比对外暗示少200亿美元，估值可信度受到质疑。
市场极度依赖AI股：2026年标普500涨幅约70%来自芯片股，英伟达权重达8.06%，澳大利亚近九成家庭通过养老金间接暴露其中。
report.impact: 对AI行业而言，这种融资模式让算力扩张速度超越真实收入增长，估值锚点变得模糊，一旦市场情绪转向，回调可能沿着投资链连锁传导。对开发者来说，短期算力和模型能力仍会快速供给、价格可能继续下降，但依赖单一供应商生态的中小团队要警惕上游资本收缩带来的服务与定价波动。对普通用户，AI产品会更便宜更好用，但养老金与指数基金通过英伟达等权重股间接承担了泡沫风险，退休储蓄的波动性上升。
report.tools: 想持续跟进，可关注：英伟达10-K/10-Q中的投资与担保披露、CoreWeave财报、OpenAI收入口径争议、澳联储《金融稳定评估》；技术侧可用Epoch AI的算力与成本数据、MLPerf基准，以及vLLM、SGLang等开源推理框架，评估单位token成本与真实需求是否匹配。
